result.title: How Mozilla uses GPT-6 Cyber to find and fix Firefox vulnerabilities
result.description:
Mozilla is combining decades of security engineering with AI agents to strengthen Firefox’s defenses.

Brian Grinstead joins OpenAI’s Clint Gibler to discuss how the team prioritizes investigations, tests and verifies vulnerabilities, finds related bug patterns, and helps engineers develop fixes. They also explore how GPT-6 Cyber revealed that some known bugs could be more serious than initially understood, helping inform which issues need attention first.

Across its security workflow, Mozilla saw about an 8× increase in bug discovery and fixes from 2025 to 2026. Brian shares what the team is learning and its ambitions for the future of browser security.

result.title: Cyber at the Frontier: Introducing Daybreak Red Team & Daybreak Defense Factory
result.description:
Greg Brockman, Nancy Wang, Fouad Matin, Clint Gibler, Alexander Thiemann, and Matt Boyle took the stage at Cyber at the Frontier, where OpenAI introduced two cybersecurity products under one unified Codex plugin called Daybreak:

Daybreak Defense Factory: builds on Codex Security Cloud to help teams automate the defensive loop to find, validate, and fix vulnerabilities at scale. It gives engineers proposed patches with test results so they can review changes before merging. All of the work runs in isolated cloud development environments.

Daybreak Red Team (early access): uses fleets of agents to test a running application within limits your team sets. It finds new vulnerabilities and checks whether an attacker could exploit issues you’ve already flagged. Engineers can send confirmed findings to Daybreak Defense Factory for help fixing them, then use Red Team to check that the fixes work.
